limitations: CUA screenshots are in the task transcript; no standalone screenshot files are claimed.
Tests ran in Windows ARM64 Parallels with x64 app emulation. No H1-H4 hardware qualification.

Final UI-only build changed NumberBox input handling after the full 86-check functional run; native hash is unchanged. WinUI packaged managed assembly hashes are recorded separately from the test harness assembly hashes.
Keyboard-only commit, other locales, high contrast, mixed DPI, other numeric editors and animation frame-time measurements remain unverified.

preservedFailures.description: Initial WinUI compile failed: incorrect StartingRequest property name and IsEnabled on StackPanel; corrected using StartPosition and ContentControl.
Test harness omitted self-contained x64 runtime; fixed harness publishing. Not an app playback result.
Actual GUI 50% input + Apply kept previous 25%, reproduced twice. Reading NumberBox.Text alone also failed; final implementation uses pinned template InputBox and regional INumberParser.
Two regressions failed before inward rounding and sample-domain coverage merging. One source sample was incorrectly advertised as two output samples.

unresolved: Actual loopback tone quality FAIL. Earlier capture attempts also contain >=50ms silence; no verified cause/fix yet.
Dynamic video capture quality fails in some attempts. Fixture rendering stalls must be separated from capture-induced repetition.
Actual microphone and simultaneous two-device capture, audio device loss/permissions, presentation cover audio exclusion, long-run clock drift and physical A/V alignment remain unverified.
Audio acquisition and disk writing still share a worker; bounded writer queue/latency handling and high-quality resampling/limiter remain to implement.
Final UI input latency, video/audio playback alignment, accessiblity, mixed DPI and broader numeric-edit input review remain.
Region capture, remaining UX, sharing/access control, signed installation/update, H1-H4 hardware, 14-day beta and independent release review remain.
